notes: Jev decision interface on the TypeSafe API (POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone; models listing GET /v1/models). Text only. Choice up to 255 options; Score at least 2 levels (API accepts up to 10); max questions per request is NOT documented (the fan-out page says adding questions usually has little effect on response time; the cookbook uses 13; one independent user saw flat latency to ~50 questions at <=4k state). No native abstain or unknown output: docs recommend an explicit "other" / "none of the above" option. No rationale text. Not fine-tunable ("the same weights serve every account"). Known limits listed by TypeSafe: counting, numeric precision, date arithmetic, indirection, irrelevant state (accuracy falls), adversarial state, option order (leans toward the first Choice option), generation. Rate limits 100K tokens/s and 80 requests/s. Context: "64k tokens per request; 32k tokens for state plus the longest question" (OpenRouter lists 32,000; Cloudflare blog says "Jev's 32k").

surfaces.notes: total_tokens 64000 and state_tokens 32000 are the "64k" and "32k" figures in the docs (state plus the longest question). Score levels 2-10. Choice and Score answers carry a `confidence` derived from the distribution; Noul has none. Confidence = (p_max - 1/n)/(1 - 1/n) per TypeSafe, which differs from Cloudflare and Perplexity definitions. Calibration is a vendor claim (RLCD); independent measurements: Decision Index ECE 0.074; Bonn pooled choice ECE 0.028; Ibrahim median ECE 0.157.
OpenRouter serves Jev at POST /api/v1/systemone (TypeSafe shape) and /api/alpha/decisions; listing context_length 32000, max_completion 28,800; price $0.042/M, completion $0.
